proposed.sourceName: Darul Iftaa Mahmudiyyah (Lusaka, Zambia) — Fatwa #1297 (Mufti Bilal Pandor)
proposed.paraphrase: Holds that bread containing L-cysteine is doubtful (mushbooh) and should be avoided unless the source is verified, because E920 may be derived from human hair or pork; it is permissible only when sourced from bird feathers, halal animals, or vegetables.

proposed.sourceName: Islam Q&A — Fatwa 248124 'Ruling on eating foods that contain L-cysteine (E920)'
proposed.paraphrase: Rules L-cysteine permissible to consume regardless of source (including human hair) because it undergoes a chemical process (istihalah) transforming it into a different, pure substance; cites the European Council for Fatwa and Research (Fatwa 34) and the Islamic Fiqh Academy's medical council.

researcherNote: E920/unspecified seeded lenient grade 3 (contested). Kept contested: the istihalah permission (Islam Q&A) is real but the source-dependent avoidance (Zambia) keeps it doubtful. Two independent tier-1. APPROVED by owner 2026-07-01 (batch pre-approval).
